artifacts.notes: Uncorrected OCR used only as a locating aid for four comparisons: the resumption rubric printed after the Twenty-third Sunday after Pentecost, which this witness carries in wording matching the 1962 Missal apart from its internal page cross-reference (445 for 422) and the grade Semiduplex; the note fixing the Ember Days by the third Sunday of Advent, the first Sunday of Lent, Pentecost Sunday, and the feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross; Additiones et Variationes, De occurrentia et de translatione festorum, n. 6, on resuming an impeded Sunday's Mass within the following week; and the same Additiones et Variationes on the pre-1960 ceiling of orations, which must not exceed seven and must keep an odd number. It controls no published wording and no page-image collation was performed.
artifacts.rights_basis: The Internet Archive item carries no license, rights statement, or public-domain determination, and names only an uploader address. Neither the underlying printing's status nor any redistribution basis for this exact OCR derivative was established, so Triptych records the exact remote bytes and retains no payload.

edition.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites, decree of 25 July 1920 declaring the Vatican edition typical; approval leaf of Francis Joseph, Archbishop of New York, given 8 December 1942, reciting conformity to the typical edition and to the decree of the Sacred Congregation of Rites of 9 January 1942
edition.notes: Superseded identity: an earlier revision of this record treated the witness as wholly unidentified because the Internet Archive item metadata supplies only an uploader-supplied title naming 1947 and no publisher, date, or rights fields. Reading the scan's own opening leaves corrects that. The title page names Benziger Brothers, Inc., New York, and the edition's relation to the Vatican typical edition (editio IV iuxta typicam Vaticanam, a Pio X reformatum, Benedicti XV auctoritate vulgatum); a copyright line reads 1942 and 1944; an approval leaf subscribed by Francis Joseph, Archbishop of New York, is dated 8 December 1942 and recites conformity with the typical edition and with the decree of the Sacred Congregation of Rites of 9 January 1942; and the Congregation's decree of 25 July 1920 declaring the Vatican edition typical is reprinted. The date field therefore records 1942 for the approved setting. The exact printing year of the scanned copy is still not established and the item's 1947 is uncorroborated; the directory slug is retained unchanged to avoid breaking existing bindings. This is a licensed publisher's edition conformed to the 1920 Vatican typical edition, not that typical edition itself. The scanned text carries the pre-1955 general rubrics with the double, semidouble, and simple grades, so it witnesses the state of the rubrics before the 1955 simplification and before the 1960 code. Being a Missal, it carries no Breviary rubrics and no tables of occurrence or concurrence. Do not merge this record with the sibling edition.catholic-church.missale-romanum.benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962: both are Benziger Brothers editions of New York, but that one is a 1962 edition iuxta typicam conformed to the 1960 code, and this one is the earlier editio IV iuxta typicam Vaticanam carrying the pre-1955 rubrics. Their divergent readings of the September Ember Days are exactly what distinguishes them.

work.description: The Roman Rite altar book containing the Order of Mass, the temporal and sanctoral cycles, Commons, votive and Requiem Masses, and related rubrical and ritual material. Edition records distinguish the authoritative typical edition from publisher-produced editions made according to it.
